> **Status: DRAFT – Not uploadable or runnable until all blockers below are resolved.**
>
> This file documents every artefact that is **CLI-owned enrichment** — meaning
> it must be supplied or generated by the UiPath CLI (`uip`) and associated
> tooling, **not** invented or hand-authored. Attempting to fabricate these
> values will produce an invalid or silently misbehaving process.

---

## Blocker 1 — Connector Resource Key

| Field | `uipath:connectorResourceKey` on `Task_SendSlackDigest` |
|---|---|
| Current value | *(absent — intentionally omitted)* |
| Why missing | The resource key is assigned by UiPath Integration Service when the Slack connector package is published/registered in the target tenant. It cannot be known offline. |
| Resolution | Run `uip integration-service connectors list` (or equivalent) against the target tenant to retrieve the registered Slack connector resource key, then inject it into the serviceTask attributes. |

---

## Blocker 2 — Connection ID / Connection Binding

| Field | `uipath:connectionId` on `Task_SendSlackDigest` |
|---|---|
| Current value | *(absent — intentionally omitted)* |
| Why missing | Connections are live, tenant-scoped objects in Orchestrator. The ID is issued when a Slack connection is created by an administrator. It is never a static or derivable value. |
| Resolution | Create or look up a valid Slack connection in Orchestrator → Integration Service → Connections. Copy the connection ID and bind it to the task either via `uip` CLI or UiPath Studio. |

---

## Blocker 3 — Connector Operation ID and Metadata

| Field | `uipath:operationId` on `Task_SendSlackDigest` |
|---|---|
| Current value | `operationIntent="PostMessage"` (human-readable intent label only) |
| Why missing | The precise operation identifier (e.g. `slack.chat.postMessage.v1`) is part of the connector manifest and is assigned at connector publish time. The intent label in this file is a documentation hint, not an executable value. |
| Resolution | Use `uip integration-service operations list --connector <resource-key>` to list available operations and retrieve the canonical operation ID. Replace the stub with the real value. |

---

## Blocker 4 — Dynamic Input Schema (Connector-Generated)

| Field | `ioSpecification / dataInput` on `Task_SendSlackDigest` |
|---|---|
| Current value | `DI_SendPayload` stub with `name="payload_STUB"` |
| Why missing | Each connector operation exposes a dynamic JSON Schema that is generated by the CLI from the connector's OpenAPI/swagger descriptor. The exact property names (e.g., `channel`, `text`, `blocks`, `username`, `icon_emoji`) and their types are defined there. |
| Resolution | Run `uip integration-service schema input --connector <resource-key> --operation <operation-id>` to generate the authoritative input schema, then replace the stub `dataInput` definitions and input mapping expression `STUB_CLI_MAPPING_REQUIRED`. |

---

## Blocker 5 — Dynamic Output Schema (Connector-Generated)

| Field | `ioSpecification / dataOutput` on `Task_SendSlackDigest` |
|---|---|
| Current value | `DO_SendResponse` stub with `name="response_STUB"`; `DataObject_SlackResponse` declared opaque |
| Why missing | The connector operation output schema is likewise dynamically generated. The `SlackResponse` variable is declared opaque in this draft because its property names (e.g., `ok`, `ts`, `channel`, `message`) cannot be reliably inferred offline. |
| Resolution | Run `uip integration-service schema output --connector <resource-key> --operation <operation-id>` and apply the result to the `dataOutput` definition and the `SlackResponse` DataObject type. |

---

## Blocker 6 — `bindings_v2.json` Entry

| File | `bindings_v2.json` (project root — does not exist yet) |
|---|---|
| Current value | *(file absent)* |
| Why missing | The `bindings_v2.json` manifest is generated by `uip` during the pack/publish flow. It records the connector binding, operation, and schema fingerprint for the Integration Service step. It cannot be hand-authored without the actual connector and connection identifiers. |
| Resolution | After resolving Blockers 1–5, run `uip pack` (or the equivalent Studio publish step) to auto-generate `bindings_v2.json`. Commit the generated file — do not edit it by hand. |

---

## Blocker 7 — Package and NuGet Metadata

| Files | `*.nuspec`, `project.json` package section, assembly version |
|---|---|
| Current value | *(absent — not part of a BPMN-only draft)* |
| Why missing | Package metadata (package ID, version, dependencies list including the Slack connector NuGet package reference) is managed by UiPath Studio and the `uip pack` CLI. These values depend on the resolved connector resource key and the target runtime version. |
| Resolution | Open the project in UiPath Studio or run `uip pack` to generate the package manifest. The connector NuGet dependency will be added automatically once the binding is resolved. |

---

## What You Can Do Now (No Blockers)

The following work does **not** require CLI enrichment and can proceed
immediately against this draft:

- ✅ Review and iterate on the BPMN flow shape (start → prepare → send → end)
- ✅ Author the `Task_PrepareDigest` XAML / workflow logic
- ✅ Define the `DigestConfig` input contract (channelIds, lookbackHours, title)
- ✅ Design the `DigestPayload` Slack Block Kit structure
- ✅ Add error boundary events or compensation logic to the BPMN
- ✅ Write unit tests for the Prepare Digest step

---

## What Must NOT Be Done Until Blockers Are Resolved

- ❌ Upload or publish this process to Orchestrator
- ❌ Deploy or run the process in any environment
- ❌ Invent / hard-code connection IDs, folder keys, or tenant URLs
- ❌ Invent connector resource keys or operation IDs
- ❌ Hand-author `bindings_v2.json`
- ❌ Copy connector schemas from another project (schemas are operation-version-specific)
